USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

Renal accumulation

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 76-year-old woman taking gabapentin for postherpetic neuralgia develops marked sleepiness after an illness causes acute kidney injury. Her dose has not changed, and liver tests are normal. Which pharmacokinetic change best explains her new symptoms?

  1. Induction of CYP3A4
  2. Increased biliary secretion
  3. Increased renal clearance
  4. Reduced renal elimination
  5. Increased hepatic activation
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Reduced renal elimination

Gabapentin is eliminated unchanged by the kidneys; impaired clearance can cause accumulation.

Understanding the options

Reduced renal elimination
Gabapentin is eliminated unchanged by the kidneys; impaired clearance can cause accumulation.
Increased hepatic activation
Gabapentin does not require conversion to an active hepatic metabolite.
Induction of CYP3A4
Hepatic enzyme induction is not its main elimination pathway.
Increased biliary secretion
Greater elimination would not explain accumulation.
Increased renal clearance
This would lower exposure rather than raise it.
